claims.text: Residual interfacial strain from deposition produces magnetic-domain pinning centers in nanoscale non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons.
These pinning centers govern magnetic-domain dynamics.
Strain-induced domain pinning increases magnetic hysteresis under low applied fields.
Strain-induced domain pinning reduces the magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
As-deposited samples possess residual stress and interfacial defects arising from rapid deposition.
The as-deposited nanoscale samples have a poorer magnetocaloric response than bulk forms.
A controlled low-temperature post-deposition anneal can reduce interfacial residual strain without significant grain growth or phase transformation.
Reducing residual interfacial strain lowers the density of defect-associated magnetic pinning sites.
Reducing strain and pinning-site density modifies magnetic-domain sizes.
Strain relaxation improves interfacial coupling relevant to magnetic and thermal transport behavior.
Lower residual stress reduces domain-wall pinning.
Reduced domain-wall pinning decreases coercivity and hysteresis losses.
Strain relaxation enhances heat-transfer rates across interfaces.
Reduced magnetic pinning and enhanced interfacial heat transfer produce a more efficient and robust magnetocaloric response during low-field cooling cycles.
Annealed samples will have lower coercivity and narrower hysteresis loops than as-deposited samples under identical low-field cycling conditions.
Annealed samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric temperature change or isothermal entropy change than as-deposited samples under identical low-field cycling conditions.
Interfacial phenomena dominate magnetic behavior in the nanoscale films and patterned nanoribbons covered by the hypothesis.
The proposed mechanism applies around the material's Curie temperature and at low applied magnetic fields, where heat-transfer limitations are significant.
